approach: Partial failure becomes a first-class property of the run boundary. One observation point tells the caller whether any record failed and how many, while successful runs keep today's contract.
elements: run boundary -- exposes success vs partial-failure outcomes to the caller
failure accounting -- knows how many records failed in a run
success path -- reports success exactly as today when nothing failed

decisions.decision: Expose the failure count on the run boundary, not via logs or a side report.
decisions.rationale: Acceptance requires the number be available to the caller of the run; a side channel makes them go looking. Revisit if a dedicated observation API becomes required.
rejected: Logs only -- caller of the run does not see the number

coverage.acceptance: A run where every record succeeded is distinguishable from one where any record failed
coverage.delivered_by: run boundary -- distinct success and partial-failure outcomes

coverage.acceptance: When any record fails, the number of failed records is reported to the caller
coverage.delivered_by: failure accounting -- surfaced through the run boundary

coverage.acceptance: A fully successful run reports success exactly as it does today
coverage.delivered_by: success path -- today's success reporting unchanged

risks: Callers that treated partial failure as clean will observe failures at cutover; this design does not stage that.
